chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Salih said:

They wanted to sell the dates of the spring of Abu Ziyad, so I wanted to buy them, then I said, 'Until I seek permission from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).' So I sent a Muṣāḍif to ask him, and he said, 'Tell him to buy them; if he does not buy them, someone else will buy them.'

key_terms.عَيْنِ: Spring/source (metaphorically referring to a date palm grove or source of produce)
key_terms.مُصَادِفاً: A messenger/envoy (specifically one who carries a message and returns with a reply)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying goods from a specific owner with the Imam's permission?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* under the chapter of trade (*al-Makasib*), this hadith illustrates the practical application of seeking the Imam's guidance (*istidhn*) in commercial transactions to ensure validity and avoid uncertainty. It highlights the Imam's role in clarifying ownership rights and market dynamics, affirming that if the primary interested party declines, the opportunity naturally passes to others, thereby preventing market stagnation.
